name: Pirriya
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only classification/endangerment refs (Breen 1990: 'Pirriya = Dormant'; Dixon 2002; Bowern & Atkinson 2012); no descriptive phonology found.

sources.citation: Breen, Gavan. 1990. Salvage studies of western Queensland Aboriginal languages. Pacific Linguistics B-105. Canberra: ANU. Chapter 2 'Pirriya' pp.6-21, sec. 2.2 Phonology p.8 (PDF p.20)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Pirriya. Sec. 2.2 gives Table 2.1 'Pirriya phonemes' and minimal pairs and says 'The sound system of Pirriya is quite likely to be the same as that of Kungkari (see 3.2.1)' -- 3.2.1 is the Kungkari phoneme inventory. The stress sentence in the book ('Main stress is on the first vowel of a word..', 3.2.2 p.26) is about Kungkari (kuun1236), not Pirriya; ch.6 p.~150 'primary stress was normally, probably always, on the first syllable, as in neighbouring languages' is about Yanda.
